chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who gives his wife the choice, or her father, or her brother, or her guardian, he said: “All of them are in the same position, if she consents.”

key_terms.أَبَاهَا: her father as a potential delegated representative
key_terms.أَخَاهَا: her brother as a potential delegated representative
key_terms.امْرَأَتَهُ: his wife in the marital legal context
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: in the same legal position or status
key_terms.يُخَيِّرُ: gives the choice or authority of decision

ai.seo_question: Are the wife, her father, brother, and guardian legally equivalent when a husband delegates marital choice?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about delegating the choice in a marital matter to the wife or to those connected to her, such as her father, brother, or guardian. The Imam عليه السلام states that these options carry the same legal standing when the wife is consenting.
